title: let Err(e) = h.await is unfamiliar to most Rust devs; needs a comment
description: The pattern 'let Err(e) = h.await;' (irrefutable never-type destructure) is non-obvious to contributors unfamiliar with the ! type. The existing comment explains it ('outbox_worker is -> ! and never returns Ok; only a panic produces Err here'), which is good. However, a contributor who has not seen this pattern before will still reach for a match or expect a compiler error. The comment is present but could add: 'Result<!,JoinError> has an uninhabited Ok variant so this pattern is exhaustive — the compiler verifies this.' The gap is small since the comment already exists.
